summary: Build reusable data products, MEAL dashboards, and responsible decision workflows for humanitarian and social protection programs. Enrol today.
lede: Data products and embedded analytics help humanitarian and social protection teams turn programme data into evidence for operational decisions. For MEAL practitioners, analysts, and programme teams, the course addresses the practical task of making fragmented reporting data useful in programme reviews and adaptation. Participants practise defining data products, profiling and modelling data with SQL, checking quality, and building decision-linked dashboards while considering privacy controls and feedback workflows.
audienceIntro: This course suits professionals who connect MEAL evidence, data operations, program delivery, and accountability across humanitarian and social protection settings. It supports beginner to intermediate practitioners who can bring a real reporting, monitoring, or decision-use case to the exercises.
audience: Social Protection Program Managers using analytics
modules: Data Modelling with SQL and dbt
prerequisites: You should have working exposure to MEAL, monitoring and evaluation, humanitarian information management, social protection delivery, program reporting, or data analysis. Basic spreadsheet skills and comfort reading tables will help. No programming background is required, and the exercises use guided SQL examples rather than requiring software development. Advanced analytics engineering, machine learning, and enterprise architecture receive conceptual or operational coverage, not technical engineering treatment.
